claim: In the matching retail DLL, instance WeaponMan.Drop(Int32 idx, UnityEngine.Vector3 p, Single gy, ZoneEnum zone, PlDirEnum dir) (0x06006AC9) has raw MethodDef row 1c5443000000860000cf0a00b8370300ad4d, RVA 0x0043541C, signature blob 2005010811190c11a85c11a768, and an exact 33-byte fat-header body SHA-256 edcc7cf0273d8a9e58e2e252323436fb039630779892b4c0e2e9654eddab7f76. Its exact flow is: local0 = this.GetWeaponObj(idx); if UnityEngine.Object.op_Implicit(local0) is false return; otherwise local0.Drop(p, gy, zone, dir); return. The GetWeaponObj call at IL+0x0002 is canonical FACT-0192. Exact matching-DLL scanning finds one direct inbound reference only, Player.DropWeapon (0x06004EDF) at IL+0x0051. Fresh R6 contains 923 Player.DropWeapon executions and no WeaponMan.Drop rows: 912 begin with recorded weaponIdx=-1 and have no nested Weapon.Drop; the remaining 11 begin with nonnegative recorded weaponIdx and each contains exactly one direct nested Weapon.Drop PRE/POST pair with matching owner slots, equal parent PRE and child PRE weaponIdx, unchanged child weaponIdx, and parent POST weaponIdx=-1.
